# 1.2.47 - projects on the map, and evidence you can actually read

The largest release since the theme landed, and most of it is the same shape:
something the module already knew was being kept in two places, or was being
shown in a place too small for it. No rule changed except where a rule is named
below. The copy is still the copy - its rewording comes with 1.3.0.

## Projects stand on the map

A project is a thing somebody is building in a room, and until now the only
place it existed was a row in a tray. It has a token now, placed where the room
is, sized larger than a student and tinted by how far along it is.

**A token you have not found is not on your map.** The whole secrecy of the
feature is one predicate asked on each client, because a Token document reaches
every browser whatever its ownership and Foundry's own `hidden` flag means "GM
only" - it cannot say "these three players". So the document carries a neutral
name, a neutral image and one id, and who may see it is decided per client from
two facts the module was already keeping: the countdown's own ownership for a
secret project, and the record of which rooms each character has stood in for a
public one. Walk into the room and the project is yours to know, from then on,
wherever you are. The entry in the Projects tab goes through the same gate: the
class could previously read the season's plan off a sidebar without leaving
their chairs.

**Observe finds what somebody is hiding.** A secret project in the room you are
searching can be found by the non-obvious declaration - "something out of
place", which is what a concealed project is - against DC 18. That number is
not new: it is the guide's own table, `hidden` visibility crossed with the
`prep` column, because a secret project is a concealed preparation. It is that
declaration and no other on purpose: a check on every Observe turns a DC 18 into
a matter of time, and a clue found by attrition is a clue the GM cannot plan
against. Finding it puts you in on it, the same way the killer brings in an
accomplice, and a Reroll takes it back with the dice.

Whether an indirect murder's rig should be findable this way is a question for
a table rather than for a file. Today it is, because one rule with no exception
is the only kind that stays honest, and because a student noticing the killer's
preparations is the game working. A GM who disagrees takes it back.

## Evidence stops being cut in half

The card a player puts in front of the table during a Class Trial lived in the
notice tile in the bottom-left corner, which is 430 x 220 and cannot grow: it
shares that corner with Foundry's tool rail, and every larger size was measured
taking the rail's own glass away. An objection carrying a Truth Bullet with its
analysis and the objector's comment needs 459 pixels. What reached the screen
was a name, four badges, and nothing else.

Evidence takes the middle of the map now, which is the one part of the screen
nothing else is using while the table argues. Two cards at a time, because an
objection answers a presentation and reading the two together is the move. It
sits one below Foundry's own window layer, so a ballot opened on top of it is
still reachable.

**And the card carries what analysis bought.** The type on it has always been
the type its presenter sees - an unanalysed bullet presents as Neutral and an
analysed one as what it turned out to be - but the sentence Analyze pays for was
not on the card at all, although the presenter's own item window has shown it
since 1.2.46. A player who had paid for it could not say it with the evidence in
front of them. Another holder's copy is untouched: knowing is per character, and
hearing something in a trial is not the same as having analysed it.

## The Event panel is in both themes

It was Stained Glass only, so that Monokuma Legacy stayed exactly the look it
was. What that bought was two implementations of the same four facts and a
Legacy screen missing information outright: no card for the opening roll, none
for a Despair overflow, and a "body found" row that vanished the moment the
investigation started. There is one implementation now and both themes draw all
of it. The clock is a clock in both, with the same one-line date and the same
phase stamp.

Two new cards, and neither keeps any state of its own:

- **The scene is stopped.** The safeword's sticky card is right for the moment
  it lands and gone ten minutes later, when the one state that means "nothing
  happens now" is on nobody's screen. The panel says so for as long as it is
  true. Who called it is not on the card and cannot be - that name never leaves
  the GMs.
- **The vote is open.** A mode of the trial's own card rather than a second one,
  so there are not two gavels in the panel. Everybody is told the vote is
  running; only a GM is told how many ballots are back. How anybody voted is not
  here and is nowhere.

Every card also lost its header line, which read "Chapter 1 - Day 3 -
Afternoon" while the clock 300 pixels away said the same thing. With three cards
up that was four copies of six words on one screen. The freed line carries the
motive's consequence, which until now lived only in a tooltip: unreadable on a
shared screen and unreachable from a keyboard.

## Truth Bullets

- The pack groups and sorts itself: this chapter first with the rest foldable,
  newest first, and a switch between grouping by chapter and by room. Both
  behave identically.
- Where a bullet was picked up is on its badge row.
- **Faint is a type you find out, not a label you are handed.** It used to be
  printed on every copy from the moment it was made, which told the holder
  something the trace had not given up yet. It is in the answer key now and
  published only when the bullet is identified.
- Tags are gone from the module. They were derived text nobody could correct;
  what replaces them is a GM changing a trace's type from the dashboard, which
  reaches every copy's answer key without telling anybody who has not analysed
  it.
- Discarding an item leaves a Resolution trace rather than a Prep one when the
  body has been found, because that is when people throw things away.
- The badge row stays inside its frame.

## Measured, and then fixed

**What the theme costs.** The stutter was chased with the Long Animation Frames
API rather than guessed at: the dominant cost is the curtain's full-screen
backdrop filter, which is paint rather than script and is recomputed whenever
anything animates. Three optimisations were tried and refuted by the same
measurement - a separate static blur layer, `contain: paint`, and
`will-change: transform` - and all three are written into the stylesheet so
nobody retries them. `game.drpg.perf()` and `game.drpg.whySlow()` take the
reading where it is real, at the table on a machine with a GPU. The script side
is single-digit milliseconds everywhere it can be measured; a no-change curtain
pass went from 23.1 ms to 4.1.

**Three self-referential measurements in the curtain**, each one something
measuring itself through a distortion it had applied:

- A column was any two blocks within 34 pixels, which merged the Despair rail
  with the status strip whenever they came close - and a column of neighbours
  cannot be cut into sections, so both lost their own glass. Every desk width
  from 1200 to 1327 reported sixteen block failures.
- The right-hand column's pin was read off a tab rail still wearing the previous
  pass's rotation. A fresh load hid it; a window resize did not converge at all.
- The curtain's own frame was read off a width the curtain had written, so
  growing the window left a bare strip of map down the right wall.

All three are fixed and the self-check is clean from 1248 pixels up. Below that
it still reports failures and it is telling the truth: the Despair rail and the
right-hand column physically overlap there, because one is centred and the other
is against the wall. That is a layout decision, not a geometry one, and it is
written up rather than papered over.

## Smaller

- The notices window is larger, and the tile is drawn on the glass that is
  actually under it - the two were sized on different scale factors and had not
  even shared a bottom edge.
- During a murder the interface's edges turn red for everyone in the incident,
  the GM, and the third party who walks in on it - and for nobody else. The same
  people, and only they, hear the murder playlist. An indirect murder tells its
  killer nothing at all: they are somewhere else, and the victim is the one who
  rolls.
- The Key Remnant planner says what is on the map. Its room and visibility
  pickers were stamped with a default into every row, so a clue placed as Subtle
  read "Evident" in its own row, and the control did nothing either way.
- Polish that stops speaking about one student in the plural, and stops assuming
  who is holding the controller.
- The evidence pack has a harness of its own (`audit/pack-harness.html`), beside
  the curtain's.
